crime: She had never carried her own weight in the prison — duties traded away, heavy work pushed onto whoever was closest, never a word of thanks.

For half a year, the girl who held the entrance-hall sweeping turn had worked around her every morning — swept past her feet, shifted her chair without a word, never once looking at her. One morning she spoke to the sweeper for the first time: said good morning, gave her own name. The girl swept on without breaking stride.

That evening the entrance hall was empty. She pushed the stone figure forward on its plinth, shove by shove — each push within her own strength, but the summed labor more than any single body could sustain. She set a wedge beneath it, in the path the morning broom always swept.
Across the lounge and the shower room, a heaviness settled into every girl's limbs at once; a few sank where they stood.
She came to the lounge afterward and sat reading at the far end. The heaviness still hung on them; it passed within the hour. One girl it had never touched, her pages turning at a steady pace.
At the morning sweep the broom caught the wedge, and the stone figure toppled onto the sweeper.

Scrape marks arced across the plinth — the trail of a heavy mass pushed along its surface. That labor could not have been sustained by a single body, yet it had been done. That same evening, heaviness had fallen on every girl in the prison at once.
When the toll of a labor falls on every girl but one, the labor is hers. The heaviness had passed over one girl — she had sat reading in the lounge, in front of them all, while they sagged.
fields.epitaph: Every girl in the prison carried her. Not one of them ever carried her name.
fields.epithet: Borne by All, Beheld by None
execution: A broom-arm geared to a chain drum on the stand — its one drive-weight an open iron case hung by the chain in a shaft, still water at the bottom.
A guard binds her upright inside the case and draws the latch at the shaft's lip.
The hung weight frees the pawl. The broom-arm begins its first row across the court floor.
Each swept row pays a length of chain off the drum; the case drops by that length.
The court follows the broom across the floor. The water closes over the cased girl.

magic.name: Debtless
magic.text: Whatever labor she performs, the physical toll leaves her body and settles on every other girl in the prison. She bears none of it.
